clue.text: George is having to engage a professional entertainer

indicators.note: to engage here means the three words take hold of the answer inside them, across their joins

explanation.surface: George is obliged to hire a paid performer for the party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to engage' looks like hiring, but it signals that the answer sits inside 'George is having'.
explanation.definitionFit: A geisha is a Japanese hostess trained in music, dance and conversation, paid to entertain guests.

clue.text: Nasty person as it happens flipping rode off!

indicators.note: flipping turns the word over so that it reads backwards in the down light

parts.note: something broadcast as it happens is going out live

indicators.note: off signals that the letters of rode are gone off, jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims in disgust that a horrible person rode off just like that.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' looks like a mild British oath on the surface, but it is the reversal signal, and 'off' (as in rode off) is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrongdoer, someone who commits wicked acts, is a nasty person.

clue.text: Strong drink for senior XV staggering inside

indicators.note: inside puts the jumbled number within the two letters for senior

parts.note: Sr is the standard abbreviation for senior, as after a father's name

indicators.note: staggering suggests letters reeling about into a new order

parts.note: XV is fifteen in Roman numerals, and a rugby team is a fifteen

explanation.surface: A strong drink is given to the senior rugby fifteen as they stagger in.
explanation.walkthrough: XV is read twice over: Roman fifteen, and a rugby team (a fifteen). 'staggering' rearranges the spelt-out number and 'inside' sets it within SR.
explanation.definitionFit: A stiffener is a slug of spirits taken to brace oneself, a strong drink.

clue.text: Harry Martin's county town

indicators.note: to harry is to harass or disturb, so the letters of the name are disturbed into a new order

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A man called Martin comes from a particular county town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry' looks like a first name beside Martin, but it is the anagram signal. ANTRIM is one of Northern Ireland's six counties.
explanation.definitionFit: Antrim is one of the six counties of Northern Ireland, in its north-east corner.

clue.text: Steep drop in dodgy videos in Sunderland?

indicators.note: in places the jumbled letters within the two letters for the region

parts.note: Sunderland is a city in the North East of England, abbreviated NE; the question mark flags the example

indicators.note: dodgy means suspect or unsound, so the letters of videos are put into a different order

explanation.surface: Sales of shady videos in Sunderland have fallen sharply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dodgy' is the anagram signal and 'in' the container; the question mark marks Sunderland as just one example of a place in the North East of England.
explanation.definitionFit: A nosedive is a sudden plunge, as of an aircraft or prices falling fast.

clue.text: Two-thirds of 20 after remapping

parts.note: 20 is RESULT; remapping its letters gives the historic province of Ulster, whose nine counties include six forming one part of the UK

explanation.surface: Someone redraws a map and keeps two-thirds of an area.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference must itself be rearranged: RESULT reshuffled is ULSTER, the old Irish province of nine counties, six of which make up this part of the United Kingdom.
explanation.definitionFit: Six of Ulster's nine historic counties form the UK province, so it is two-thirds of the old province.

clue.text: Fallow fields make the easiest ground around Land's End

indicators.note: around puts the jumbled letters on both sides of the single letter
ground means crushed or milled, so the letters of easiest are broken up and reformed
End picks out the final letter of Land's

explanation.surface: Leaving fields fallow makes for the easiest ground near the tip of Cornwall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' rearranges EASIEST to SETASIE, and 'around' wraps it round D, the last letter of 'Land's'. Land's End is the far south-western tip of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Set-aside was the EU scheme paying farmers to leave arable land uncultivated, so fallow fields.

clue.text: County town, short of water, invaded by "English" king? No, besieged

indicators.note: invaded by means the other letters push their way into the word for waterless

parts.note: something short of water is dry
E is the standard abbreviation for English
R stands for rex, Latin for king, as in royal signatures

explanation.surface: A thirsty Irish town is attacked by an English king, though in truth it was besieged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No, besieged' corrects the picture: the 1689 Siege of Derry was laid by the deposed James II, not an invasion by an English king. DERRY is the Irish city also called Londonderry.
explanation.definitionFit: Derry is the city that gives its name to County Londonderry, so a county town.

clue.text: Wantonly damaged London museum, then told stories out of school

parts.note: the V and A is the Victoria and Albert Museum in London

indicators.note: out of here means the word for fibbed lies outside the single letter

parts.note: telling stories is a mild way of saying lied

explanation.surface: Someone who damaged a London museum then sneaked on others at school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' has LIED around S. 'Told stories out of school', an idiom for gossiping, hides the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To vandalise is to deface or wreck property deliberately and for no reason.

clue.text: What body snatchers do, more than half with indifference

indicators.note: more than half keeps eight of the eleven letters, losing the tail

parts.note: disinterest is a lack of concern, indifference

explanation.surface: Grave robbers go about their work with little more than indifference.
explanation.walkthrough: 'more than half' keeps the first eight of DISINTEREST's eleven letters, dropping EST.
explanation.definitionFit: Body snatchers dug up fresh corpses, and to dig a body out of its grave is to exhume it.

clue.text: Power's run out in river

definitions.note: the possessive points to the first name belonging to the actor Power

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation within the river's name

parts.note: the Tyne is a river in north-east England
ro is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for run out

explanation.surface: Power fails as something runs out into a river.
explanation.walkthrough: Tyrone Power was a Hollywood star of the 1930s-50s, so 'Power's' name is wanted; it is also one of Northern Ireland's six counties. 'in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Tyrone was the forename of the 1930s-50s screen actor surnamed Power.

clue.text: Fletcher's work Footlights also rejected in recession

indicators.note: in recession means withdrawing, so these letters go away from the theatre word
rejected sends the word back, so it reads in the opposite direction

parts.note: too means also

explanation.surface: A Footlights comedy by Fletcher is turned down during an economic slump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns TOO into OOT, and 'in recession' takes OOT out of FOOTLIGHTS. A fletcher makes arrows; Footlights is the Cambridge University revue club.
explanation.definitionFit: A fletcher fits arrows with their feather vanes, which are called flights.

clue.text: OK to ban knife from Jewish school

indicators.note: to ban here means barring those letters from the school word

parts.note: a yeshivah is an Orthodox Jewish college for Talmudic study
shiv is slang for a knife

explanation.surface: It's agreed that knives are banned from a Jewish school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to ban' removes SHIV from YESHIVAH (a variant spelling of yeshiva).
explanation.definitionFit: Yeah is an informal yes, signalling agreement just like okay.

clue.text: Tragic Prospero as a U H banished king? Not in A R these productions

annotationWithheld.why: Tragic Prospero as a U H banished king? Not in A R these productions (4,6): stray grid letters 'U H' and 'A R' are in the clue as held; the clean clue is an anagram of PROSPERO AS A less R (king), but the fix is beyond an OCR misread and there is no scan
annotationWithheld.clue: Tragic Prospero as a U H banished king? Not in A R these productions

clue.text: Blue clue?

definitions.meaning: feeling blue means feeling sad or low
the question mark points to a clue answered in a vertical light, as opposed to an across one

explanation.definitionFit: Being low is being depressed, and a vertical crossword clue belongs in the second list.

clue.text: Expo's paying producers more after reordering parts

indicators.note: after reordering parts swaps the two halves of the phrase, so the second comes first

parts.note: fair trade schemes pay growers in poorer countries a better price

explanation.surface: An exhibition is paying its producers more after reorganising its sections.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after reordering parts' swaps the halves of FAIR TRADE. ''s' stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: An expo is a large exhibition, and one where businesses display goods to buyers is a commercial show.

clue.text: County consists of fen replanted with 25

indicators.note: replanted means dug up and put down again, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the answer to 25 across is the name of another Northern Irish county

explanation.surface: A county consists of marshland replanted along with a neighbouring county.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue should read 'fen'; 'replanted' rearranges FEN with ARMAGH (25 across) into a single new name.
explanation.definitionFit: Fermanagh is one of the six counties of Northern Ireland, in its south-west.

clue.text: Bird overcomes urge to gossip

indicators.note: in a down clue the bird word comes over and around the urge word

parts.note: a chat is a small songbird, such as the stonechat
an itch is a restless urge

explanation.surface: A bird overcomes its urge to gossip.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'overcomes' can mean one piece goes over the other; here the bird wraps around the urge.
explanation.definitionFit: Chitchat is light idle talk, the same as gossip.

clue.text: In it, apparently a third got mistreated round Cape ultimately

definitions.text: In it, apparently a third got mistreated round Cape ultimately

indicators.note: got mistreated signals that the letters are handled roughly into a new order
ultimately here keeps only the later part of the word, losing its opening letter

explanation.surface: Under South Africa's old system, apparently a third of people were mistreated around the Cape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' takes the end of 'Cape', APE, and 'got mistreated' rearranges A THIRD with APE. As a whole the clue describes the regime.
explanation.definitionFit: Apartheid was South Africa's system of racial segregation under which the non-white majority suffered.

clue.text: Banner headline features big bird

indicators.note: features says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A newspaper's banner headline is about a large bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhea is a large flightless South American bird related to the ostrich.

clue.text: Consequence of addict being hauled up in front of officer

indicators.note: being hauled up in a down light means read from the bottom upward

parts.note: a user is a drug addict
Lt is the abbreviation for lieutenant, an officer

explanation.surface: The consequence for an addict is being hauled up before an officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being hauled up' turns the addict word upward in this down light; 'in front of' sets it before the officer.
explanation.definitionFit: A result is the outcome that follows from an action.

clue.text: Huge photograph attached to email?

parts.note: the e of email stands for electronic and is prefixed to other words
pic is short for picture, a photograph

explanation.surface: Someone attaches a huge photo to an email.
explanation.walkthrough: 'attached to' joins PIC to E, as an image attached to an email is an e-pic.
explanation.definitionFit: Something epic is on a grand, heroic scale.

clue.text: Son avoided poor handwriting stroke

indicators.note: avoided means the letter for son is kept out of the word

parts.note: a scrawl is messy, careless writing

explanation.surface: A son avoided a teacher's stroke for bad handwriting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'avoided' drops S from SCRAWL. 'stroke' suggests a pen-stroke, but it is a swimming stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: The crawl is the fast front swimming stroke, also called freestyle.

clue.text: Article about South American girl

parts.note: the is the definite article
re means about or concerning
SA abbreviates South America

explanation.surface: A newspaper article about a South American girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Theresa is a female given name, so a girl.

clue.text: See 2
County town near Maghera (ignoring the Border)

indicators.note: ignoring the border means dropping the outer letters of the phrase and keeping the inside run

explanation.surface: A county town lies near Maghera, if you ignore the Irish border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Border' looks like the Irish frontier, but it means the outer letters of 'near Maghera'. Maghera is a town in County Londonderry.
explanation.definitionFit: Armagh is the cathedral city that gives its name to County Armagh, a principal town.

clue.text: Big fan distracted alto in Wagner's A major …

indicators.note: in puts the muddled letters inside the German key name

parts.note: A-Dur is German for A major, as a German composer would write it

indicators.note: distracted means thrown into confusion, so the letters are muddled

explanation.surface: A big fan is distracted by an alto singing in Wagner's A major.
explanation.walkthrough: Wagner was German, so his A major is written A-Dur; 'distracted' is the anagram signal and 'in' the container.
explanation.definitionFit: An adulator heaps praise on someone, an ardent admirer.

clue.text: … solo as Isolde tremblingly embraces amorous Tristan originally

indicators.note: embraces means the shaken letters hug the other two inside them
tremblingly means shaking, so the letters of the heroine's name are shaken up
originally picks the first letter of each of the next two words

explanation.surface: Isolde sings solo, trembling as she embraces an amorous Tristan, in Wagner's opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tremblingly' rearranges ISOLDE to ISOLED, which 'embraces' AT, the first letters picked by 'originally'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being alone, set apart from others, is the state of acting on one's own.

clue.text: Top Hirst shocked Tate's chief

indicators.note: chief means head, so the leading letter of the gallery's name is taken
shocked means jolted, so the letters of the artist's name are jumbled

explanation.surface: Damien Hirst's latest work shocked the head of the Tate gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chief' takes T from 'Tate's'; 'shocked' rearranges HIRST to SHIRT. Damien Hirst is a British artist known for shock works.
explanation.definitionFit: A T-shirt is a short-sleeved casual garment worn on the upper body.
